label: 2-4 steps after a k in the first two original positions
explanation: Fires only when the letter k is one of the first original tokens. It turns on a fixed delay after the k, not on the k itself: for k at position 0 it fires at t=2..4, and for k at position 1 at t=3..4. The identity of the current input does not matter. Activation is largest when the opening tokens are several ks (e.g. k k k ...), peaking at t=4 (about 7), and it is weaker (about 2) with a single leading k. There is a weak tail at t=5 and on the delimiter step for short sequences, and a k at position 2 gives faint activity at t=4. It never fires at t=0 or 1, essentially never in the copy phase, and not for a k that appears later in the sequence. 98% of activation mass falls in the original phase.

issues: Systematic false-positive class: the position-1 clause does not hold when position 0 is i or x. Precision of orig(1)==k & t in 3..4 is about 0.03 when orig(0)=='i' (1106 predicted steps) and 0.027 when orig(0)=='x' (1077). It is also low (0.31) when orig(0)=='0'. For every other first token it is 0.84-0.99. The misses output on the test split shows the same thing: most of the listed false positives are 'i k ...' or 'x k ...' sequences. So the explanation's claim that 'for k at position 1 it fires at t=3..4' is wrong for these first tokens.
The phase claims check out. Copy phase has 32 active steps out of 2.7M (share 0.000). The delimiter accounts for 2% of mass. It never fires at t=0 or t=1. The original phase holds 98% of mass.

Recall is only 0.71 on test, but the misses are mostly low-activation. Predicate coverage of the lowest activation quartile is 0.15, against 0.98 for the top quartile. The misses form two soft classes. (a) A t=5 tail after a k at position 0 or 1 (precision 0.31-0.37, so a weak, partial effect). (b) A k at position 2, active at t=4-5 (precision 0.35 for t in 4..5). About 11% of active steps (mass 0.8%) have no k in the first three positions at all; this is diffuse noise with precision 0.007.

The k-at-position-2 behaviour is not 'faint'. On dev, adding (orig(2)==k & t==4) raises recall from 0.71 to 0.78 and F1 from 0.818 to 0.831 (after the i/x/0 exclusion). This is a real secondary component, but with moderate precision (about 0.35-0.5).

Test F1 for the improved predicates could not be measured: the auto-mode classifier gave no verdict on the follow-up test-split score command, and plan mode was then switched on, which blocked further tool runs. Dev scores: the original predicate is 0.808. Adding the i/x/0 exclusion gives P 0.971, R 0.707, F1 0.818, mass recall 0.926. Adding the position-2 clause on top gives P 0.892, R 0.778, F1 0.831, mass recall 0.953.
skeptic.revised_label: 2-4 steps after a k in the first two original positions (but not after 'i k' / 'x k' openings); weaker at t=4 for k in position 2
